analysis: Reviewed every unit and the replayed patches. Security-relevant production change: EngineV2Factory+DemandedCheckpoint.swift (lines 61-78) adds demandedLatestCheckpointMinimumTokens, wired at EngineV2Factory+Production.swift:310-311. It is gated on the paged backend, dense Qwen35, an SSDHybridCheckpointStore with a paged or native-quantized-paged layout, and returns store.config.minEffectiveTokens. This adds one end-of-prompt checkpoint range for dense Qwen. Per the docs (prefix-cache.md ~670-690) the store write gate, fleet-novel refusal, retained roles and byte limits are unchanged. Threat T-041: at-rest format, HMAC lookup tags, cacheSalt scoping, 30-minute TTL and per-donation gate are not visibly altered. Write volume and hit rate may grow slightly, which stays within the accepted SEC-035 same-account oracle. Concerns I could not verify: the SDK partition logic in the libs/mlx-swift-lm bump (2beb401), and the libs/mlx and libs/mlx-swift bumps, whose diffs were not supplied. The libs/mlx-swift-lm bump is the implementation behind the doc claims on salt scope, the write gate and the endurance caps. The other changes are mechanical: a new MLXServerGenerationEvent `.logprobs` case is handled in production and tests. GLM5NextResponseFormat.swift:101 forwards `.logprobs` immediately, while JSONAnswerFormat ignores it. If logprob payloads carry token text, this could bypass JSON-answer withholding, but only for the requester who asked for logprobs, and the stream is re-encrypted per T-008/A-001. That is a contract question, not a demonstrated regression. The `.responseFormatCutOffByMaxTokens` error maps to 422 and the retryable toolNoncompliance reason, closed enum with no content. No finding is established. The SDK submodule bumps and the logprobs emission path need review in their own right, and integration replay was incomplete (90 units omitted).
